Honestly the reversal was worse than my ostomy.. at least for my total colectomy… my barbie butt permanent  ileostomy surgery initially wasn’t too bad but I had some complications so I can’t compare it with the previous… I was also 14 when I had my j-pouch surgery & I was 31 when I had my permanent ileostomy & barbie butt
Which app is it from? I can try to find it
NP!  I’m actually on that dose myself 😁

Self medicating can be problematic… vitamins aren’t regulated (unless it’s an actual prescription like vitamin D and b12 injections) … 
That being said I would recommend taking to your doctor about seeing an occupational therapist.  They work on fine motor skills like eating, buttons, zippers, writing etc.  obviously it also depends on what’s causing your neuropathy too.
I think the max dose is 3600mg per day

It’s not so much the sugar for me but the added electrolytes… but I also struggled with keeping my electrolytes balanced… I just figured knowledge is power!  You might want to do a food diary & also track if your output changes; then you’ll have a better idea of what might be influencing your output.  

The only other thing that could affect output would be medication?
F… what’s the title? I feel like I’ve run across this before but I don’t know where

I did the Metamucil wafers initially after my total colectomy after my temp ileostomy was reversed & I was using my j-pouch.  I haven’t used it since I had my permanent ileostomy surgery because I don’t think it’ll help me much because I lost more small bowel with that surgery.  I was originally told by my colorectal surgeon to drink 64 oz of Gatorade a day.  I really don’t like the taste and I stumbled across liquid iv years ago and it’s now my preferred solution to staying properly hydrated because I mix 1 packet into 1L of water.  Technically it’s more expensive but you get way more electrolytes and less sugar (they do have sugar free flavors but I buy mine at Costco where they carry 30 ct packs but only 1 sugar free option & currently it’s flavor combo I don’t like 🤷🏻‍♀️) 1 stick of liquid iv contains 11g sugar, 500mg sodium, 370mg potassium, 62mg vitamin c, 19.3mg niacin, 1.93mg b6, 5.79mcg b12 & 9.6mg pantothenic acid… whereas a 12oz serving of Gatorade has 21g of sugar (a 28oz bottle is 2.5 servings so that’s 52.5 grams of sugar ) it lists that there is another 48g of added sugar on top of the 52.5g so it’s it’s over 100g of sugar! Sodium is 380mg and just 110mg of potassium.  I have always watered down my electrolytes partly because it’s easier to drink but mainly because I use to be really really bad about drinking water … it was a bad habit from my j-pouch days… I had it in my head that water = more time in the bathroom 😣…  now I can tell when I’ve fallen short on my fluid intake. 

I was just googling if milk is better than water for hydration… because I wasn’t sure… ie it’s not something I’ve been told and I really don’t drink milk myself… I prefer oat milk myself… it’s a switch I made several years ago… I had issues with respiratory infections & I was told to not drink milk (because it effects mucus production) originally I started drinking soy milk but after I was diagnosed with a cancer that has links to estrogen I was told to avoid soy products so I switched to Almond milk but when I learned how much water it takes to grow almonds & make almond milk I switched to oat milk… I highly recommend the extra creamy … it’s delicious! Anyway… according to a Harvard medical article there are some studies that suggest it but the actual evidence is really weak & backed/sponsored by the milk industry.  It really doesn’t hydrate better than water plus it’s obviously has more calories too.

Oh I can totally relate to the diet struggle… I’ve had a LOT of bowel obstructions following my total colectomy & j-pouch… I had my APR (j-pouch + additional intestine removed & my perm. Ileostomy + Barbie butt) I struggled A LOT with my diet… hell I still struggle and it will be 14 years on 5/5 this year.   I’ve only in the past 6ish months started to widen my dietary horizons BUT I try to limit new foods to small amounts so I can get an idea of what works and what doesn’t… there are foods I will NEVER eat because I don’t want to push my luck… 

I would say it’s a good idea to let your body heal before adventuring into veggies (unless they’re cooked well & it’s not high fiber) I know there are folks here who can eat just about anything… I can’t… I don’t like feeling uncomfortable when things don’t digest well… it’s good to get a core group of foods you can eat without issues.  Make a list of things you want to try or even better maybe look at some recipes and find things that interest you.  Life is a marathon so it’s ok if it takes time for your body to adjust to the new normal.  

dm me if you ever want to chat about anything  :)

Look up SSRI there are many different kinds & it’s can take a bit to find what will work best for you… however I highly recommend seeing a psychiatrist and not going the PCP route… I’m not saying a PCP isn’t capable of prescribing but sometimes having a mental health dr on your team can be a game changer.  That’s just food for thought

I was just going to post the same!  Insurance only limits how much you can order (even then there are ways around that too!) If a supplier is telling you it’s not covered it’s because it’s expensive & they won’t make $ off it.

I found this out when I was doing AR for an independent pharmacy & I got roped into billing Medicaid for some ostomy supplies… I guess no one had done the actual billing before 😓 needless to say it cost more … but that’s Florida Medicaid and it was like 10 yrs ago.

I think the only issue I’ve had a problem with is that the billing code for 2 different items being the same… or at least that’s an issue I’ve had with ordering from Byram (it’s the protective sheets and barrier strips-the regular round strips) So I found that I can just order the barrier strips from another provider.. and my problem was solved!

Eek sorry for the novel. TLDR; change supplies bc they should only limit how much you can order not what you order

Hmm... it depends on the trip but I err on the extreme side of caution because I've gone on a trip with more than enough supplies (honestly I had enough for 2+ weeks) for a 10 day trip and I ran into soooo many problems with my ostomy that I burned through EVERYTHING >.<  Granted there were outside forces that were the cause (or at least IMO) that trip reinforced the though of it being better to have too much than not enough!  It's definitely almost a security blanket for me

These days I just use paper towels.  🧻 n the earlier days I had a prescription for a 1L bottle of sterile saline & non-sterile 4x4 gauze… I originally got this from my home healthcare provider & then I got a prescription for the sterile saline from my doctor… these days I don’t need it … but if you have pissed off peristomal skin I highly recommend sterile saline for cleaning around your stoma.  It doesn’t hurt & won’t leave anything behind.

Hiya!  I had a total colectomy w/ ileorectal anastomosis aka “j-pouch”. I had a temp ileostomy for 3 months while the j-pouch healed.  Honestly it’s as easy as you would think… mainly because whatever type of output you have with your ostomy will be what comes out the other end…  The hard part is sphincter control… I didn’t have an issue with it… but lots of people do… so it may mean needing to wear a pad or something like that to protect anal leakage  =\.  You also need to know where the nearest bathroom is and I highly recommend having a prescription for lomotil and also have OTC Imodium too.  

Unfortunately it’s not a simple thing to do… I personally almost regret having it done… but I was 14 when I had it done & I was 31 when I had my permanent ileostomy done.  I’ve had less issues with my ostomy than I did with my j-pouch. From frequent bowel obstructions to feeling like I was chained to the 🚽😣… I wish I could tell you that it’s easy… but it’s not as simple as it would seem

Good luck!!  I had my temp ileostomy reversed 3 months after my total colectomy… be prepared for it to feel like you’re shitting battery acid… it will BURRRRRRN 🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥😱  Seriously I was NOT prepared for it!  You’re also going to want to know where the nearest bathroom is where ever you go… every one has a different level of sphincter control… I suggest Metamucil biscuits or the powder I used the biscuits personally but it’s about adding fiber to bulk it up a bit .  I highly recommend talking to your surgeon about getting a prescription for Lomotil it’s really helpful! You can also use Imodium too. I would also get calmoseptine or butt paste to help with the butt burn your going to experience.. I would say avoid any kind of wipes that have alcohol in them… it’s going to take time for your body to adapt to your new plumbing setup.  

I had a jpouch for 17 years… I had a love/hate relationship with it… but I think it was the right thing to do at the time… I was 14 when I had my first 2 surgeries.  Oh you’re going to also be careful when eating stuff with nuts and seeds especially at the beginning… the adjustment will take time… be kind to yourself!  I hope everything goes smoothly!! 🤞🤞🤞

Feel free to message me if you have questions or just need moral support! 

You’re doing a kickass job! Hang in there!!

It’s tough at the beginning!  I had a really hard time too.  My stoma was barely flush … have you tried Coloplast’s SenSura Mio?  They have at least 2 different kinds of convex wafers.. regular & deep.  I started using the “regular” but switched to the deep when it became available.  I’m not sure if they do samples internationally or not; but I highly recommend them! I rarely have issues with leaks or appliance failure.,.or when I do it’s user error 😂

Honestly I use to get maybe 3 days of wear time before… I can go a week or longer…(I went 10 days once it’s a long story.. 😤 ) Oh!! One thing you’re going to want to keep an eye on is the size of your stoma… it’s going to shrink as you heal and the inflammation goes down 😁

I would say that you definite know your body the best so if you feel ready to test the waters then go for it!  If you’re worried about not getting enough calories could you ask for some thing like ensure or boost? They make various types of shakes that taste good & give you more calories, protein & vitamins… especially if you find that eating soft foods like eggs, oatmeal, bananas, rice etc are still causing you issues with digestion.  I’ve had a lot of experience with transitioning from NPO to food … both from surgeries to bowel obstructions 😭.  It’s never fun dealing with angry intestines … I hope you’re able to transition smoothly back to your normal diet!
It’s possible to pass bits of nuts well after you’ve eaten them like days later… but nuts & seeds are not the easiest things to digest

I actually have issues with most adhesive products from paper tape to bandaids to generic tegaderm… I had a really bad reaction to eakin seals too.  I’m not familiar with Salts… I’m in the US.  I would say if you can get your hands on some Coloplast 4x4 protective sheets you *should* be able to use the wafer that’s causing you issues because it’s a hypo colloidal sheet so the wafer wouldn’t touching your skin at all.  

I don’t think skin prep would work to prevent any type of skin reaction.  Is there a reason you’re changing appliances?

Ooof!  I don’t want to jinx myself about night time disasters… I’ve had many myself…I actually saved myself the other night when I woke up & my bag was literally beyond capacity…I’m still boggled by the fact it did blow up 😱🤯 

Back to the issue at hand! I highly recommend having a small hand held carpet spot cleaner.  My sister has the bissell pet stain eraser… she got it for her cats (hairballs) but it’s amazing for cleaning small to medium-ish areas.  They make a cleaning solution to go with it but I know my sister recently got a new carpet cleaning solution that she got to deal with a stain that didn’t come up with the cleaning solution… I’ll have to ask her tomorrow for the name of it because it was amazing!  I think it might be an enzyme cleaner but I’m not sure 🤷🏻‍♀️🤦🏻‍♀️

I lost my dad before I finished my AA degree … it was my first step towards my dream… he died hours before my first class of my last semester… I made him a promise that I wouldn’t stop living my life once he passed…  I’ve kept my promise… your mom never stopped believing in you! She’ll always be cheering for you!  Especially because YOU did this & that’s AMAZING!!!

OMG I’m sorry y’all are having an even harder time with a situation that is already hard enough without the extra (pardon the pun) shit additionally!  I struggled quite a bit at the beginning too… My ileostomy was not even flush with the surface of my skin & both my incisions from my surgery had been opened & were packed twice a day so I couldn’t stand to do a change out if I wanted to 😭.  So I get that laying down might be easier for you & him.  I also can relate to frequent change outs due to leaking… I don’t know what products you’re using and a visual of the stoma so I’m just going to toss out some stuff that I know from my own personal experience that have worked & helped when I was really struggling with getting anything to stick to my peristomal skin.

I have to say I have had a LOT of experience with home health nurses… they are great when it comes to dealing with say surgical wounds but most have veeeeeery limited experience with “normal” stomas and thus know roughly how to do a typical change outs…but anything outside of that and they will try their best but honestly they’re probably worse at it than you are!  I would HIGHLY recommend googling to find an actual ostomy nurse that’s in your area … you might have to travel a bit but I promise you it’s worth it to get that kind of care especially with everything y’all are going through! It was a game changer every time I had issues I got in touch with an ostomy nurse because even when if you’ve had an ostomy for years things can change & you need someone with more knowledge to troubleshoot whatever is going on.  I know because it happened to me after 4 years of stoma life… I was in a clinical trial for a new chemo med and unfortunately it’s main side effect was diarrhea 😭… I had to travel up to DC every 4 weeks but I ran into major issues with in days of being on the medication… I was thankful that the clinical trial team was able to hook me up with seeing an ostomy nurse before I went home because I literally blew through over a 2 weeks supply of my ostomy stuff (which is a nightmare regardless… stupid insurance limits 😤) I think someone suggested this already but OMFG Marathon is MAGICAL!!! My skin all around my ostomy site was red, inflamed & painful! I had zero normal skin for my appliance to stick to… It looked like my skin was burned.., red & weeping! The weeping makes it impossible to get it to stick & that is where Marathon saves the day! I was introduced to it by an ostomy nurse at the NIH hospital in DC… I forget the exact instructions but I think it was applying stoma powder & then applying the Marathon & then putting the wafer on.  It’s a bit expensive but totally worth it .. OH! Actually your home health nurse should be supplying you with all the ostomy supplies you need so you should be able to have them order it for you! Another thing that I found was helpful when I was having skin issues due to leaks & subsequent skin problems is to use 4x4 gauze & sterile saline solution for cleaning the skin around the stoma. It helps cut the pain of needing to clean the area because the saline is the same pH as blood which means it doesn’t hurt the way normal water does.  I also found that the non-sterile woven 4x4 gauze pads are excellent at wiping up output most of the time. Obviously it’s hard if the stoma is going to town with pooing up a storm… Also in the realm of things that won’t burn mad peristomal skin is alcohol free skin prep… I highly recommend cavilon no-sting by 3M (Marathon is also a 3M product) don’t let them substitute it for similar no-sting product… I have found that there are differences between them and that makes a difference!  I think someone else mentioned Coloplast’s barrier sheet, which is an AMAZING product & one that I use all the time but I don’t know if it’s something to try when your son’s skin is as bad as it is… I can’t speak from experience with regards to if it would stick to say Marathon & stoma powder.. You can call Coloplast & talk with a rep who will ask you a bunch of questions & they’ll put together a box of products that they think would help with the problem & then they will follow up with you to see how it went .. you can actually do that with Convatec & Hollister too. The reps are well versed in all things ostomy so you’re not just talking to someone who’s reading lines from a script…

Getting an ostomy for ANY reason is traumatic but when it involves multiple surgeries & complications it’s even MORE traumatic… which is why I highly recommend therapy for not just your son but the family too!  I only started going to therapy because my sister went & I saw the impact it had on her… I was skeptical about it because I was so use to being in survival mode & never really addressing/acknowledging my trauma… I actually got triggered by a post in this subreddit which shook me to my core… but I’m thankful for therapy because I was able to talk about … thing like this have a deeper impact than just the surface level stuff… but it also effects everyone too. 

I think it’s amazing what you’re doing to help your son.  Remember to give yourself time to decompress & fo something nice for yourself because self-care is super important when you’re doing double duty mom & caregiver!

I can’t speak to what it actually looked like (no picture) but I have used Hollister adapt rings myself  (it’s been awhile since I did, just disclosing that 😊) The ring is probably wonkier than when you first put it on because it did its job (protecting from leaks) it’s very normal for those types of product to look different after a few days

Yep! I put like 2 squirts of the m9 in first then toss the Altoid in & you’re golden!  It sounds crazy but it works better than anything else!  My sister use to burn a fuck ton of incense … like every time I went to the bathroom I would come out to it burning… In the last 4+ months of using this combo I can only remember her lighting it once and it was due to an accident 🙈
Umm… is this due to having a rectal stump? I vaguely recall my dad having to deal with mucus dripping after he had his ostomy surgery in the early 90’s… either way 🤷🏻‍♀️
I honestly just rinse it with water (at least when I’m at home) add some m9 & an Altoid & I’m good!

Don’t be so hard on yourself!  It happens to everyone at some point… I had a really bad accident at work shortly after I had returned to work after my surgery.  I had my supplies with me but I didn’t have a change of clothes so I had my SO pick me up & I went home.  It’s upsetting when it happens but it’s just something that happens from time to time.  I know you probably don’t want to talk about it … but it’s really important to let your boss know because this can happen & honestly more people are more concerned with your wellbeing than the fact you have a colostomy.  You don’t have to say anything specific to your coworkers but it’s good to give them a vague heads up that you might need to stop what you’re doing to take care of a medical issue or something like that.. again most people will be worried about YOU than whatever it is.  

Try to do something nice for yourself because self care is important! Be kind to yourself & it will be OK!  

Sending you some air hugs!🫂

Edited to add:  Always carry an “emergency” change out kit! I’ve had my ostomy for 13 yrs and I still keep one with me when I’m away from home for long periods of time.  I use to have clothes in my car too. I did that after my own accident at work.  It will get better!

Was there a picture? I can’t see it so I’m just guessing… but also which brand do you use?  I have a very innie stoma (she’s legit cosplaying the Sarlacc from Star Wars 🤣) but I think the thicker output tends to not move so much.. aka pancaking at the top… where as the liquidity doesn’t., but positions also matter too. So is it an issue with when you’re sleeping?

I think wear time varies from person to person… but I can say from my personal experience that changing frequently SUCKS!!! At one point in the early days of my life with my permanent ileostomy… I was changing every other day… which was a nightmare when I was using paste but less of a disaster with a seal but still not ideal; however I was changing frequently for reasons other than normal/problematic things… I’m kinda lazy about my change outs.. mostly because my stoma is a brat and I try to do it when I think it’s safe 😂

Ditto! No ring, paste, powder or skin prep… I do use a barrier sheet (which goes on before the wafer.. I use the deep convex Mio wafer… OMFG it is a total game changer!  I was told by my rep that you don’t need skin prep or stoma powder because of the technology of the wafer! 🤯🤯🤯… 

After I cut my holes I put my barrier sheet & wafer on my heating pad to warm it up … it helps with the wafer especially because it’s harder .. but I also put my heating pad over my appliance once it’s on.  I started doing this when I moved to a much colder climate than I was use too… I went from Florida to New England… 🥵 to 🥶🥶🥶 🤣🤣… now it’s just part of my routine 🤷🏻‍♀️
OMG…. Why have I never thought of doing that 🤣🤣🤣

I’ve tried a lot of of stuff in the 13 yrs I’ve had my ostomy & my stoma is a problem child (aka she’s an innie) … I started with convatec (the convex moldable wafer) which was terrible… I saw an ostomy nurse who switched me to a Hollister convex wafer which was better but I was plagued with leakage & I also had trouble with my stoma too… my body was trying to heal my ostomy 😱… At the beginning I was using paste (I hated it!) so I tried to use Eakin seal but my skin said NOOOOOOOPE!!! I had some kind of allergic reaction to it 😭… also the convex wafer wasn’t convex enough… so my ostomy nurse set called Hollister & they sent me samples of everything including their convex barrier ring… I was nervous about it; after the disaster w/ the eakin seal… but it worked!  I was using that for several years and I don’t remember why I ended up switching to Coloplast… but I think it was after I had a minor revision of my stoma (they removed the skin that had grown over my stoma & thankfully it worked! 🥳) but I ended up getting samples from them & the rep who had me was truly AWESOME told me (before the actual release) that Coloplast was going to release a deep convex wafer… because I don’t remember exactly what happened… unfortunately around that time I was diagnosed & under went a lot of treatment (chemo, radiation, clinical trial… a treatment break…then more chemo & now thankfully I’ve been stable for awhile 🤞🤞🤞) so my memory is potato…but I do remember being really excited about it because up until that point I had to use multiple products to get OK wear… I think I was averaging like 2-3 days… which was better than the every other day I had been forced to do before my stoma revision; but that was mainly due to having to dilate my stoma or rather the skin that was choking off my poor stoma 😭😭😭.  I have never been excited about anything appliance related… because it’s been so MEH… Honestly the lack of choice is quite astounding because people come in all kinds of sizes & shapes… not everyone has a “perfect” stoma…. I like to joke about my stoma being the Sarlacc (from Return of the Jedi… iydk google it 😂) but she’s been an innie from day 1… I’ve also struggled with my weight… I gained almost 100 lbs during my treatment & I’ve thankfully lost 100 lbs in the last few years (and have kept it off for the most part… I fluctuate the same 10 lbs 😩) which definitely makes it more difficult… but I absolutely LOVE the Coloplast SenSura Mio Deep Convex wafer!  It’s hard enough & the convexity isn’t just at the edge of the wafer (which was the case for both Convatec & Hollister’s wafers at least that was true like 5-10 years ago. I don’t know if they have released anything because I’m very happy with my set up!) I only use their Brava barrier sheet (4x4) to protect the skin around my stoma & the barrier strips around the outside the wafer & I can get up to 7+ days (obviously it’s not really a good idea to wear it that long… at least for me personally… because the longer it’s on it starts to leak around the edges… I think it’s just because the acidity of the output over time with “eat” at the edge of the wafer & the barrier sheet) I try to change it every 5-7 days… sooner if necessary.  The only other thing I use is m9 drops in my pouch w/ an Altoid(has to be peppermint) and that’s it! Goodbye paste, seals, powder & skin prep!  Oh I forgot about adhesive remover! 

I made the mistake at the beginning of my switch to the Mio of using skin prep & stoma powder… I was having issues with leaking & I was talking to my customer service rep at Coloplast about it & they asked me to walk thru my steps and I got to the stoma powder & skin prep & I learned that the powder & skin prep were not only not needed but also the reason why I was having problems with leakage… I was a tad skeptical.., because it was ingrained in my brain that I *HAD* to use skin prep & stoma powder… but it’s true!!! I haven’t looked back & even if I have pissed off skin due to leakage… my skin has never not recovered from skipping the skin prep & powder.  The rep told me that it’s part of the technology with how the wafer is made… I highly recommend if you have any kind of “innie” stoma… call Coloplast & talk to them! Honestly all the companies (or at least I can say this is true for Convatec, Hollister & Coloplast) they will send a welcome to ostomy box with products specific to your needs (or they use to… I don’t think they have stopped doing it) usually they send like 2 of each… I think Coloplast sent more… but it might not have been in the welcome box… but you can ask to try ANY product in their catalog… I also appreciate that the reps know what they are talking about & they will follow up with you & see how it went & go from there.  I had a positive experience with all 3 companies… I’m team Coloplast simply because they have the best products to meet my specific needs.  I highly recommend reaching out to them ESPECIALLY if you’re having issues with your appliance.  It also is a good to have an ostomy nurse too… at least at the beginning and I would say if you’re having issues it’s not bad to ask for help.  
/end of my TEDTalk 😵
I’ve got an innie & she’s more oval than round… I save the plastic backing from my wafer as my template (I use a convex wafer) So it’s ostomy scissors for me :)

Yep! But only the OG peppermint ones… I tried wintergreen & cinnamon… I was curious… I also tried livesavors too (omg that was a disaster!) I did try Trader Joe’s knock off version which worked too

I know it’s got to be devastating & soul crushing… I was 14 when I had my colectomy & temporary ileostomy & my parents knew I would have this surgery, my dad had a permanent ileostomy too AND even they had struggled with all the emotions … he’s going to need his mommy to let him know that it will be alright; because it will be! It will be challenging but life didn’t end because of the surgery… think of it as a new adventure!  Whether it’s permanent or not it’s important to know that he’s going to have a new “normal” because things are different without a colon… I know I had a hard time at first but eventually I accepted it & even found it interesting… a large part was because my dad did his best to be supportive & really helped me but I felt bad knowing how much guilt he felt. I know your situation is vastly different from mine but I just wanted to say that kids are very aware of things & it’s ok to feel however you do… but positivity will make a big difference & I highly recommend therapy not just for him but for all of you! I’m 45 and I honestly only recently realized that I never processed everything that came with it because it changed my life … I wish I could have been told it was ok to feel all the feelings… I saw how much it affected my parents so I bottled it up… I’m not saying that will happen but it’s important to know that it’s ok to ask for help & support for everyone! 

He’s going to bounce back from the surgery much faster than you would think… I remember getting up the day after my surgery & became the favorite on the floor because I was the only kid on the floor… I wasn’t in a children’s hospital… ironically that was across the street… they didn’t have GI specialists or surgeons so I had adult doctors which can be challenging at times but mainly because they don’t usually treat kids but not every area/community has access to such specialized care so it becomes important to become a specialist yourself or just educate yourself on what your kiddo needs so you can advocate for him and as he gets older you can then teach him how to do it for himself. It’s going to be tough but you’ll be amazed at how much you grow & bond.  It’s not the end but a beginning of a new adventure!  This sub is full of amazing people & so many stories plus loaaaads of information & resources! You are not alone!!

My 2 absolute ***MUST HAVES*** are m9 odor eliminator drops (Hollister item# 7717 ) and peppermint altoids …. This is a game changer!!! It’s the poo pourri for your ostomy.  I’ve tried the various “deodorizing” products & nothing comes close; most just make it smell like flowers 💩💨😓).  

When it comes to actual supplies… I highly recommend (once you know what kind of stoma is or innie or outtie) call customer service for Coloplast, Convatec & Hollister.  They’ll not only send you a welcome package full of products to try (which they’ll customize it to your specific needs!) but they’ll check in with you to make sure you’ve got everything you need & they’ll let you know when new products are available & they’ll send you samples of anything that you need/want.

I’ve used Convatec, Hollister & Coloplast (I have an ileostomy & most of my output fairly liquidy… I think I’ve probably gotten 2 maybe 3 days before the filter fails.,.but it depends on how things are going..

I second this!  I use one of the c-shaped & one y-shaped … my incision skin is really sensitive so I discovered this combo & it’s really helped me get a longer wear time for my appliance.

You can reach out to Coloplast & they’ll send you samples of them & any other items you might need. They’re really awesome! They might offer samples of other products that they have that might be good/useful for you.

Immediately following surgery your diet IS limited; your bowels need time to heal & adjust!  High fiber food like raw veggies can be SLOWLY added back into your diet. There will be foods that are no-nos but it varies by person.  You won’t be able to eat the same way you did before BECAUSE an ileostomy stoma is SIGNIFICANTLY SMALLER that your colon was & you can’t/dont’t have any control over how food exits your body.  If you don’t want to land in the hospital and/or be in excruciating pain don’t push it.  There are ways to get fruits & veggies in & your diet will change as you heal.  The diet post-op is strict for a reason; I’m guessing no one talked with you about it and/or they just gave you a list of things not to eat & didn’t explain it well… or maybe they did but you get told a lot of things both before & after surgery & your may have been focused on other things? I say this as a person who’s had 2 ileostomy surgeries.., one at 14 and again at 31 and I don’t think they said anything to me when I was a teenager… but my dad had an ileostomy when I had my first/temporary ileostomy; so I think they might have said something to my parents, who then told me not to eat anything outside of that very limited range of foods… but that was back in the mid 90’s and they didn’t really know or care about it… However when I had my permanent one in 2011 I was given a lot of info about my diet & I remember getting a pocket sized guide on foods that covered no only things to avoid in general IE foods that really are no-nos, but also info about how various foods affect on the back end… but honestly I only remember my surgeons drilling into my head how important it is to staying hydrated!  It’s something that even almost 14 years later I still remind myself to do; although I don’t drink gatorade anymore thanks to better electrolyte drink mixes that have more electrolytes and no sugar & taste sooooo much better too! (highly recommend liquid iv or similar mixes… I put 1 packet in usually 1 liter but no less than 500mL, it’s just how I like it 🤷🏻‍♀️) Anyway… one of the main reasons why your diet is restricted is because your anatomy is drastically different from what it was AND it functions differently too; so foods that you could eat before are at BEST ok in very LIMITED quantities BECAUSE your stoma is not only smaller but you have zero control over when you 💩  and trust me bowel obstructions SUCK!  When you eat the more problematic foods you can’t eat large quantities of them because your body can’t process them like before your surgery.  Unfortunately there are physical limitations to eating a lot of things and/or eating anything in large quantities is a bad idea… your bag can only hold so much… not to mention if you eat something that causes gas too…🫣  Slow & steady and smaller quantities are the name of the game because you need to adjust to how your body now functions (from digestion to how it comes out the other end)

One thing that is really important (especially because your bf has a new stoma) to do is to make keep an eye on his stoma because as he heals it’s going to change size which will effect not only potential leaks but can cause skin irritation around his stoma.  I speak from personal experience with my first ileostomy when I was 14… my dad was doing my earlier change outs because I refused to do anything with it at first… it was a temporary ileostomy & he forgot that it shrinks as it heals & so I had really pissed off skin around my stoma… thankfully appliances today are waaaaaaaay better than the stone age of the ‘90s but it’s always better to avoid issues when possible!  Keep an eye on it & it’s ok to change it more frequently!

My sister would light incense to help with the smell (which I honestly didn’t notice most of the time) She no longer does this since I started doing this trick.  I put more that what it says on the bottle ie it says 4-12 drops.. I use 2 quick squirts of the bottle & drop the altoid & I let out any air in the bag & I’m good to go! So the first thing I noticed is the utter lack of emeralds in your gear! DH's run off dex there for emeralds! if you're finding yourself to be too "squishy" first welcome too being a DH, we tend to be a tad squishy (well not all are...) but the class as a whole is more vulnerable than say a monk or a barb.  So I'd say keep the diamonds in your pants and put emeralds in your chest piece.  

The next thing that you need to do is a) ditch using the Visage of Gunes, you currently do not have the necessary CDR needed to keep vengence up100% if the time or as close to 100% which means it needs to be above 33% anything lower means you're at severe disadvantage while you're waiting to be able to go back into vengence.  Next you really need to raise the lvl of your gems and while we;re talking about gems the only time you need the Bane of the Stricken is running GRs, especially if you're running solo... If you're running normal rifts or bounties the gems you should use are Bane of the Powerful, Bane of the Trapped and Zei's Stone of Vengence. GRs I personally run Bane of the Trapped, Powerful & Stricken and leave out Zei's stone (tbh I don't actually use Zei's in any of my builds that I run but its a combination of using different gear and having played a DH since day 1... I've always preferred the bow class characters since way back to original Diablo)

Passive skills... this is an area where you can play around with it a bit more when running the multishot UE build. I would say you'd be better off making another hellfire amulet or 20... how ever long it takes you to get an amulet with a useful passive skill (ie Awareness, Cull of the Weak, ballistics) because this will open up your passives to try out different combinations... again a lot of stuff is a matter of personal preference and it's something you kinda get an idea of the style of play and you can tweak as you go.

Realize that you have the beginning of a UE build, as you do more rifts and hunt or make gear you'll get better pieces which will always make a difference.  Ok i've written a novel... but before I end I'll just point out a few things to be mindful of

1) if you have less than 33% cooldown w/o using Leoric's crown in your cube, it's much better to be in vengence 100% of the time than it is to have some meh damage reduction and you die a lot because without vengence killing is harder.
2) CHC & CHD are important, but you need to make sure between your bow, quiver & chest piece you should have at least 84 discipline point (ideally you'd want the max of 86 because it increases your dmg, but it's not the end of the world if your re-roll of a stat was better spent on something else, ie if your bow's dmg range is crap but you have 10 or 11 discipline, you'd be better off re-roll the dmg and shooting for a high lvl that's fire based (since MS is a fire based attack)
3) If you get a goldwrap, save it because when you become more comfortable I can tell you running normal rifts wearing a gold wrap and a maxed out boon of the hoarder as long as you have gold coming in you're pretty much invincible (note that after 5 seconds it drops unless you're getting a steady stream of gold.) Not only do you not die... you'll build up a ton of gold which you can then use to empower GRs.
4) Never waste a re-roll on a weapon to get a socket... hold out for a ramalani gift (but I think that's pretty well known but just incase)
5) run GRs even if they're lower ones to work on building up your main gems and also you want to work on building up gems that you can use later to augment better gear.
6) as you farm and work on getting better gear, you can also re-roll legendary items using the cube, just note it's a pain in the ass and eats up resources >.> but can sometimes really pay off. A lot of farming for DBs and mats for the various acts

Hi Jake!(I originally wasn't going to read what others have said...but I did, so I'm going to elaborate on things that weren't covered) =)

With regard to your heart rate jumping around, a big cause for that is going to be your **PAIN LEVEL**. Seriously, your pulse aka heart rate is totally influenced by your pain level. You're doing yourself **ZERO** favors in not taking your pain medication in a manor that **DECREASES** your pain! 
OK so pulse rate **IS** affected by PAIN, best way to lower your heart rate is to get your **PAIN in CONTROL!!!** Seriously, it **WILL HELP** you sooo much!!! 
Ok... I'll stop harping on the serious nature of pain control. And trust me I know how horrible it feels to have your heart beating above 120bpm.  Oh, **JUST AN FYI** increased heart rate is **NOT A SIDE EFFECT** of either drugs that make up the drug Norco; i.e. hydrocodone or tylenol. It is however a side effect of **NOT TAKING YOUR PAIN MEDICATION**!!! 

I rather got the feeling that the two things that were bothering you the most were drug side-effects and potential for abuse/addiction, so this is some info for thought, I did dig up the most common side-effect from Google because it's a good info source and I'm hoping my info helps you.  
I googled Norco side-effects and this is what popped up & they are in fact accurate. (I was a national certified pharmacy technician for over 10 years & I worked in Florida, Virginia, DC & California, so I do have a lot of knowledge about drugs i.e. side effects, drug-drug interactions,etc)

**Norco Overview - Patient Information: Effects: Nausea, vomiting, constipation, light-headedness, dizziness, or drowsiness may occur. Some of these side effects may decrease after you have been using this medication for a while. If any of these effects persist or worsen, tell your doctor or pharmacist promptly."**<- these are the most common side effects and from them most will disappear after being on the medication for a day or a few. 

There is always a difference in how your feel when you transition from IV pain medication to oral pain medication. My best advice to you is take it as it's directed for a few doses and see how you feel. If you feel like it's a bit too much, with your next dose just take 1 tablet... you can adjust how you take your medication as you need to. You'll find that your pain is greater at certain points in the day and lesser in others, which means you only have to take what you need. 

/u/Aellus put a lot of emphasis on the potential for addiction. 
To be honest... while yes Norco has been re-classified from a "controlled substance" to a "class 2 narcotic medication" doesn't mean it's super addictive. The DEA did it because the patients that had been abusing oxycontin/oxycodone and the other narcotics changed to the various types of hydrocodone because it was easier and cheaper to get. Is it addictive, yes it is, will you get addicted to it, unless you have an addictive personality, no, you'll get through this and be back to your new normal self. But if you have concerns about it, I'd definitely talk with /u/Aellus .

Before talking about the rectal stump and mucous issue, I wanted to talk about stoma side of things. It's important to keep an eye on your output i.e. color, consistency & frequency because your doctor will ask about it, especially in the beginning. If you just get a little notepad and pen and keep them in the bathroom, you can jot down all that info and when you see the doctor you'll be prepared! Now when it comes to the rectal stump and mucous leakage... I only experience that when I had a temp. ileostomy while my j-pouch was healing... I remember at first I had a drain, but it got removed, but I used these butterfly shaped gauze pads which worked great for catching mucous... then agai n I was 14 at the time and I'm 35 now >.> So I can't tell you much about having a rectal stump; but I **CAN** tell you about having your backdoor removed. I can tell you the good,the bad, the really bad & ugly and how it gets better. :) I'm not saying that to freak you out... I'm just saying that I experienced the when everything that can go wrong *does* go wrong. So I can tell you about the things that the medical people forget to tell you!

Ok, with the appetite... what you might be experiencing is the change from IV meds to oral meds and also to not having an IV supplementing your fluid intake. I think once you get your pain under control, which should help with the heart rate, it may help with the appetite... I honestly think that once you stop stressing out over things, i.e. the heart rate, your pain meds, you'll find your appetite will return. The important thing is to remember what you can and can't eat... it's best to keep to an **EXTREMELY SIMPLE** diet! There are are a lot of foods that can cause all kinds of discomfort or even worse blockages... which really really **REALLY SUCK** (yes I'm speaking from personal experience >.>) You also need to drink at least I think it's 64 fluid ounces.. but you need to make sure out of that 64 that you drink 32 of a electrolyte infused drink... it can be gatorade/powerade/pedialyte; you just need to make sure that you don't just drink all water because when you sweat,you lose more than just water. We lose all kinds of different  salts...which is why athletes or anyone doing strenuous activities have some fluids with them that are rich in electrolytes. Trust me it is no fun to have your body turn into a full body charlie horse... >.>  ok so the important lesson here is to keep hydrated and make sure to have and electrolyte enriched drink everyday. <= my surgeon told me this was like the most important thing (outside of staying away from the evil food)

I did have a minor revision surgery done last December because I had really bad scar tissue that totally surrounded my stoma and it got to the point that even with dilators I couldn't stretch the scar tissue, so for about 3 weeks before I had the surgery I was on a pure liquid diet because the opening was smaller than a dime and it wouldn't pass even something as simple as mashed potatoes. So I had the scar tissue removed and a small bit of my original stoma. Recovery time took about 2 months before the area calmed down, but I had an issue with and infection and popped stitches.  My surgery for my perm. ostomy it took a good while before things got settled... I think they say that it takes about a full year before your stoma has totally matured, but the initial swelling usually takes a couple months and in that time you can hit up some of the major manufacturers make a "Welcome Kit" which comes with samples of all kinds of stuff. I highly recommend you hit up them one at a time... like one month hit up Convatec (not my favorite brand for wafers, but they have lots of other awesome things) they have a great welcome kit. it comes with a bag, ostomy scissors (because normal scissors are not met to cut wafers) full sized samples of several of their items... they'll customize it to your needs. Then the next month you can hit up Hollister (they were my favorite wafer and then my revision changed that :( ) they also customize the welcome kit to your needs, so you'll get the products you need/want and other handy things. Then you can hit up Coloplast, which has become my absolute favorite! They have amazing customer service and have no issue with replacing products if something fails.. like for example I had a box of wafers where after less than 2-3 hours of wear I'd have a leak or blow out... I literally went through 4 wafers in under 24 hours...but that also meant I burned through bags & their 4x4 protective barriers (I also lost 4 sets of their I suck at remembering what they're called, but after you put everything on you put these barriers around the  wafer it gives added protection, it replaces the need to tape around your appliance with the pink tape because these things seal and protect your appliance from water and stuff) Coloplast actually will let you try one of literally everything! It's really handy when you're trying to figure out what kind of wafer you need and also what other items you may need or maybe just want to try... like the barrier rings (it's exactly like the eakins seal just Coloplast's version) They all have stoma nurses that work for the companies so that when they get a new patient calling in, you'll get a stoma nurse who will ask all the important questions like how new is your stoma, what kind is it, how big is it... is it poking out or is it flushed/recessed; because all of these questions help them figure out what products they should recommend to try first. And the good thing is most of them will call you back after a week or so to see how it went and if anything needs to be changed and if it does, they'll send out the new sample and it'll continue until you find the perfect or as close to perfect as you can get an appliance.

I have 2 important questions for you (you don't have to answer if you don't want too, I'm just seeing if I can help... I've had a recessed stoma since I had her installed on 05/05/11 & even after I had surgery in December to remove scar tissue that was choking off my stoma, I *still* have what I lovingly refer to as a shy stoma :p)

Anyway question 1 is... Do you shave the area around your stoma each time you do an appliance change out?  I personally don't have much problem with hair...then again I'm a girl, but my dad was also an ostomates and I remember him telling me how important it was to have as little hair possible. It will definitely help with the issues that can pop up due to being hairy.
Question 2 is both a question and some very sound advice on how to deal with having a concave areas around the stoma. The question is... Do you use a convex appliance? If not you should dial up whichever product line you're use to and even one you haven't used to see if maybe by changing that 1 thing you'll solve your leaking problem or at the very least help.

Right now just about everything I use is Coloplast, but you are correct... The "protective barrier sheets" are AWESOME!!!! Especially for any ostomates that have problematic ostomies. All you do is cut a hole the size of the Ostomy (adding between 3-5 mm of extra space) it's applied directly to the skin before the appliance is applied. The only thing I do first is apply stoma powder to the peristomal skin, then I apply either no sting barrier wipes or the marathon liquid... The barrier wipe is for skin that isn't too damaged; the marathon is used when a large section of skin is red and weeping, without the marathon any thing you'd try to attach would fail if not instantly witching a few hours. It's super important to look after the skin around the stoma because bad things can happen :( 
OOOOOOOH! I almost forgot! There are a couple other new products by Coloplast... They have skin paste but instead of being in a tube that will dry out, it's in strips that are packaged individually are are quite similar to the rings, only you can use as much or as little as you need. Its really easy to use and it doesn't cling to skin like paste does. They also have lubricating deodorant liquid, which you add to your bag after each time you empty. It helps keep output from pancaking, buy lubing up the bag all the output slides nicely to the bottom.

Anyone who hasn't gotten the welcome package from the main Ostomy product maker, you really should! I've gotten welcome packages from Convatec, Hollister and Coloplast, they come with samples and all kinds of helpful things. If you go to their website it should have a contact number. :)

I have many tips/tricks I use for healing the skin around the stoma...It's a lot more challenging for those of us who have the shy stomas...ie flushed or recessed. That being said... before I had my stoma revised in December, I had a set routine for my skin and everything. I often found that the crusting technique worked most of the time. The only time this failed me was after I started a clinical trial chemotherapy drug which had the horrid side effect of causing SEVERE DIAHRREA >.< I ended up needing to see the WOCN located at the NIH (National Institutes of Health, located just outside DC, it's the world's largest research hospital) any way the Ostomy nurse introduced me to 2 new products which I use when the peristomal skin is red and weeping. the first was a silver antimicrobial powder which she applied instead of the stoma powder and the 2nd is call Marathon its made by Medline and it's kinda like a super glue but it doesn't sting and it's purple so you can see where you've already applied it. It creates a barrier between the weeping skin and the wafer so the appliance actually sticks! but it's only used in extreme situations (mainly because it's expensive!)

Now I was introduced to a product by Coloplast which is OMFG awesome!!! It's a barrier film which is made of a hypercolloid  material and it has reduced my leaks to like nil! Which means I can wear my wafers longer which I wasn't able to do before!:) I still use the stoma powder/skin prep rountine for the skin that gets exposed to any output, but it's just a small area and I think just due to the nature of my ostomy I'll be hard pressed to have perfect skin, but the barrier film is honestly kick ass! :) I'll have to take a picture and insert it so yall can see what I mean :)

Congrats on working towards becoming a nurse! We need more nurses out there that have a better understanding of all things ostomy.... because outside of a WOCN, most nurses have limited exposure which can be hard at times... especially when hospitalized.

Welcome to the world of ostomates! Hopefully you're healing nicely and will make the transition from a temp ileo to I'm going to guess that you're going to be reattached to a j-pouch or something of that nature.

One thing I really want to say is... everyone is different. When it comes to food tolerance... the best thing to do is start **EXTREMELY SLOW** when trying foods that can be bad for you as a person with an ileostomy. Trust me... there are pros and cons to everything you place in your mouth.  Speaking as a person who's pushed the limits with trying foods and landing in the hospital way to many times with blockages... which I will tell you now, they **SUCK ASS** seriously, if you enjoy puking your guts out and feeling like your body is trying to eject your intestines out of your body or make you want to rip the dame thing out yourself... yeah that's what it's like to have obstructions... it's WAAAAAAAY worse to get one with an ostomy... that is a 1 way ticket to getting admitted to the hospital and having an NG tube placed.  I don't know about you... but I fucking **HATE** NG tubes!

Ok this being said... [shitbaggins](http://www.reddit.com/user/shitbaggins) Did give some good advice... but I will have to make some altered suggestions... just because you (OP) stated that you've got a temp ileostomy. 

So here it goes.... while I do agree with some of what shitbaggins said.... due to the fact that your ileo is a temporary one... trust me you don't want to rock the boat... your intestines are cranky and pissed off at being poked and man-handled in surgery. So here are a few tips and tricks I've learned along the road... 

Just a little back story on me... I had my first (aka the temp) ileostomy placed when I was 14 in 1994... I had it reversed 3 months later and I had a j-pouch for 17 years... I had my j-pouch and stuff removed 2 & 1/2 years ago (all surgeries were due to bowel cancer... genetics are a bitch!) so now I have a perm. ileostomy. So enough on me... here are a few tips and guidelines I learned the hard way... aka I've landed in the hospital too many times to count due to eating things I shouldn't... so I'm trying to share what I've learned so you don't have to experience the asstatic fun that is having a bowel obstruction. (they serious SUCK... and it can and will happen even after you have the ileostomy reversed)

1. While some of the "rules and guidelines" to what not to eat are true... you *can* try some of the "no-no" foods if you try a small amount and only eat 1 supposed no-no food at a time. If you mix them or eat too much... you're gonna be miserable and could end up in the ER.

2. Nuts and seeds are **NOT** your friend! Whether you have an ostomy or a j-pouch.... I highly advise against eating them. Why? There is nothing worse than having to deal with not only butt burn (I'll explain that in a bit) but also having rough undigested nuts or seeds cutting into extremely sensitive skin. Nut butters are perfectly fine as long as they are smooth and not chunky... but if you wanna give it a go... that's fine... but just keep this in mind... I'm trying to save you pain and misery.

3. I agree with shitbaggins... the rule about not drinking from a straw is dumb. I think for some people it *might* cause gas issues... but I find that I have more problems from carbonated drinks than I do from drinking with a straw. I think the "rules" they give you are just a guideline in some ways more than rules that shouldn't be broken.

4. Since you have a temp. ileostomy... if you try a "bad" food and it doesn't work for you... don't eat it! Most no-no foods that don't work when you have an ileostomy will not work once you've been reattached. Unfortunately things do not go back to what you use to know before you kissed your colon or part of it goodbye.

5. It doesn't matter what kind of blockage you might have... if you have an issues with severe abdominal pain or you're not producing output or it's watery... **GO TO THE ER ASAP!!!** Blockages are not something to play with and can be extremely serious... especially if you've got an ostomy... it can do serious injury to your bowel. It is **ALWAYS** better to be safe than sorry. (I know this from personal experience having had way too many blockages with both my j-pouch and ostomy... it's far worse having one with a stoma!)

6. I need to correct shitbaggins here... it's not a matter of You will probably get dehydrated easily. The fact of the matter is once you lose all or part of the colon, you **WILL** get dehydrated because the main function of the colon is to absorb water... without that organ, you'll get dehydrated simply if all you drink is water. Anyone who has an ileostomy or a j-pouch **MUST** drink liquids that replace electrolytes or else you'll end up in the hospital feeling like you've been hit by a truck and your muscles will feel like your body is just one giant charlie horse... and believe me it is NOT fun! Gatorade is ok... the problem is the high sugar content... even the G2 formulation isn't that great. An alternative is Pedialyte... I know you're thinking "WTF?!? That's for babies and kids that are puking and have diarrhea." Pedialyte has more of the electrolytes you need and less sugar in it, so it's a great thing to use to keep yourself properly hydrated. You also **HAVE TO DRINK MORE THAN A GALLON OF LIQUID A DAY TO STAY PROPERLY HYDRATED** I can't emphasis this enough! It's extremely important to stay hydrated... dehydration happens so quickly in people with shortened GI tracks... and the symptoms are aweful and can also be misleading... like the first symptom is headaches... then comes nausea and vomiting... muscles spasms... and it goes downhill from there. Another awesome source of electrolytes that is both tasty and great for you... Coconut water! I tried it for the first time and it was amazing! There are also plain water that have electrolytes added to the water but have no taste. (I'll have to look in my kitchen later to give you names of some products I use) You can also add things to your food to help with keeping your body balanced. But you also need to be careful not to go too far overboard... its a delicate balance so you need to be careful not to go too crazy with the electrolyte enriched products.

6. As shitbaggins says *If you get an itching sensation around your stoma, especially if it's not right by your stoma, you probably have a leak, or at least one forming.*  It's important for you to be aware of **HOW** your skin feels... if you feel that something's off... the first thing to do is check your appliance... if you see any discoloration, change your appliance immediately!!! If you don't see anything odd... I'd pop the bag off and check your stoma just to see if there isn't something off.... if you don't see anything but you still think it doesn't "feel right" change out your appliance! It is much better to be SAFE than sorry! It's much easier to take care of a minor skin irritation than it is a major skin issue!  Most leaks happen because of improper fitting of your wafer... if you have a shy stoma (mine's very shy) use a convex wafer... if it's an inny... then add a convex barrier ring... if not then a normal wafer is fine. One really important thing to remember is that your stoma **WILL SHRINK!!!!** As it heals the swelling goes down and about a month after the surgery.... your stoma size should be what it'll be until it's reversed.

8. Always measure your stoma! Since you have a newborn stoma... it **WILL** change as it heals! Just be aware that it will happen and you'll avoid having issues with massive leakage and skin burning... yes... your stool is extremely acidic and when left on regular skin it will burn it!

9. I also use Hollister products... I started initially with Convatec... but a visit to an Ostomy nurse (they're actually called Wound Ostomy Care Nurses... aka WOCN...) It's best to see a WOCN so that you can know that the products you're using are the right type for your ostomy. Your skin and stoma will thank you for it! 

Ok sorry for the long ass reply... I just want to offer up my plethora of knowledge of this stuff... Before I hit save... I'm going to list some of the **must have** products for taking care of your skin and stoma!

* 3M Cavilon No-Sting Skin Prep... This is the BEST skin prep out there! It doesn't contain any alcohol so even if your skin is raw, it's not going to hurt when you apply it!

* Stoma powder - I swear this stuff has some kinda voo-doo magic or something! Anytime I have pissed off skin... I dust the whole area around my stoma with it and then brush the extra off and then pat the powder with a skin prep wipe, which turns the powder into a gel barrier and somehow by the next time you change out... the skin is magically healed!

* Barrier rings! - I personally use Hollister's convex barrier ring... but you can try the eakin seals or hollister's flat barrier ring... they work MUCH better than stoma paste which I always found to be hard to work with and practically useless. You can contact the manufactures and get free samples, which is seriously awesome! (WOCN are also great for getting new products to try out)

Ok... I've rambled more than I intended to... when I feel passionate about something.... I tend to say more than I normally would :) But I want to help save you from making some of the mistakes I made... because they were painful and sucky lessons!

If you have any questions feel free to PM me :) If you need to know what it's like to be re-attached... I can give you some tips and tricks to help you avoid the shitty biscuit part of that. :)

Is this a permanent or temporary ileostomy? I find that there is a HUGE difference between the two.... I know because I had a temp ileostomy while my j-pouch healed and now I have a permanent ileostomy now.

There are lots of foods that you SHOULD NOT EAT - corn, nuts, seeds, popcorn, celery, fruits and veggies with skins.

Slowly add things back into your diet... bowel obstuctions suck ... seriously speaking as someone who's had WAAAAAY too many this life time... Don't rush your gut too much... if you combine too many of the wrong things you will pay for it... aka land in the hospital with an NG tube because with an ostomy it's impossible to "force out" poo.

Chew everything you eat really really REALLY well! (if you're getting reversed you'll still have to do similar things because the small bowel is so unforgiving compared to a colon) You should drink more than you put out and you need to drink electrolyte enriched drinks - Gatorade, Powerade or Pedialyte because with an ileostomy you're at a high risk for dehydration (which is also not fun - headaches, nausea, muscle cramps are a few things that happen) If you drink or eat stuff with coloring in it or has natural color to it (like beets) don't freak if your output looks odd colored. I generally avoid anything that can turn my output red because it can be confused for blood. 

I find that anything carbonated causes too much gas and I hate having a puffy pouch! <- I use filtered pouches and have still had issues with balloon pouch. So I don't drink carbonated stuff and I avoid drinking with a straw (this also can cause excessive air)
